pagerbot: PAGER: [auth-proxy] high 401 spike (>1200/min). Potential credential replay. Severity: P1. Runbook: auth-flood. @oncall
alex: I'm on it. grabbing logs + tracing now.
maria: seeing a sudden tail of 401s from ~185.74.23.0/24 and 45.77.9.12
alex: can you paste a snippet of the ingress logs?
maria: here: `2026-03-20T15:02:11Z auth-proxy 401 GET /v1/llm  src=45.77.9.12 user_agent="python-requests/2.28" session_id=abc123 fragment="Bearer ..."`
alex: thanks. pattern looks like repeated short-lived sessions with identical bearer fragments across different IPs — possible replay or harvested token reuse.
security_analyst: tagging in. do not rotate customer keys yet. we need to confirm scope (internal svc tokens vs user API keys). start containment: block IP ranges and throttle auth-proxy path, enable token revocation scan.
kenji: enabling deadman fallback to `auth-proxy-readonly` for affected routes to keep customer traffic from failing entirely. patching route now (2m)
maria: applied IP block for 185.74.23.0/24 and 45.77.9.12, returning 429 for repeat hits. monitoring.
csm_julia: i'm seeing 3 support tickets from AcmeCorp and two from NeoApps complaining about intermittent 401s. they flagged production job failures.
alex: quick grep across logs shows ~0.3% of total auth tokens show reuse across >3 distinct IPs within 5m window.
security_analyst: prioritize scanning S3 debug logs and CI artifacts for leaked bearer fragments. also check staging log forwarders.
kenji: starting keystore sync and planned key rotate for internal service accounts (non-customer). command: `./ops/keystore sync && ./ops/keystore rotate --target svc-auth --nonblocking` will take ~10m. I'll run now.
alex: tracing shows spike ingress at 15:01:40 -> plateaued for 6m, now dropping after IP blocks and throttles.
security_analyst: recommend emergency customer token revocation only for tokens that show cross-IP reuse and are service-account flagged. we'll prepare a limited revoke list. not a global rotate.
csm_julia: message drafted for affected customers (AcmeCorp, NeoApps). waiting on final scope to send. want to avoid mass churn.
maria: found a staging S3 shard with recent debug uploads that include `Authorization: Bearer` snippets from a CI job. notifying infra to quarantine the bucket.
kenji: keystore rotate finished for internal svcs, no customer keys touched. we left a rollback plan in `ops/rotations/2026-03-20`.
alex: mitigation status: IP blocks + throttles + deadman fallback + internal svc key rotate + S3 shard quarantine. 401 spike down to baseline. continuing monitor for 30m.
security_analyst: we'll perform a forensics job on token reuse set and finalize limited revocation list. handing off to next oncall for watch and customer comms.
pagerbot: Incident updated: status=mitigated -> monitoring. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-flood
csm_julia: sent customer note to AcmeCorp (cc legal). will follow up with timeline once we finalize revokes.
alex: handing off to night-oncall @maria. log pointers: s3://redwood-incidents/3288889999/*.trace, query id=tx3288. last_message_ts=3288890800
